description:
Found while building fz-sc8.72. resolve_module_name (src/compiler2/world.rs) returns the current module when a single-segment name equals the current module's last segment. So inside a top-level `defmodule Foo.Bar`, a bare `Bar` means Foo.Bar. In Elixir `Bar` is the atom Elixir.Bar unless an alias binds it; the current module is reachable only as __MODULE__ or by its full name.

Probe: `defmodule Foo.Bar do def me(), do: Bar end` then `alias Foo.Bar; dbg(Bar.me())`. fz prints Foo.Bar; Elixir prints Bar.

Fix at the one authority: drop the last-segment rule from resolve_module_name, then confirm with an oracle fixture that nothing in lib relied on it. Deviation from Elixir; not needed by the distiller.
title: A bare module name inside defmodule Foo.Bar is Bar, not the current module
